audit.title: Rate and Volatility Feed Addresses

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: The implied question is "what is the contract address for feed X on chain Y?" — and the served page answers none of it. The `## Networks` section is empty in the rendered markdown. Critical gap.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Only 3 headings, one an empty section, one a newsletter CTA. A reference address page should be a set of per-network tables; the harness sees **0 tables, 0 bullets**.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: An address page with **0 hex identifiers and 0 numerals in prose** is the worst possible outcome for a dimension that specifically rewards addresses, chain IDs, and decimals. This is the single most damaging finding.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Two internal orientation links present; no per-network block explorer links, no primary-source anchors. Weak.

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: No definition of what a Rate feed or Volatility feed is near first use. Nothing liftable.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Strongest dimension — 2 valid JSON-LD blocks, canonical set, `inLanguage` correct, 12 OG + 9 Twitter tags. Weaknesses: `datePublished` == `dateModified` (never-revised / generator-stamped), `keywords` are auto-generated with stopwords ("for", "and"), and all 4 `about` entries use the templated "Content about X" pattern — low-signal entity data.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: No code, and for a pure address-listing page that is largely acceptable — but a copy-pasteable example of reading one listed feed would help. Neutral.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Devs and agents query "chainlink [asset] rate feed address on [network]." The page targets that intent by URL but delivers no matching body content. Fails the query it's built for.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: The little prose present is clean, but the newsletter CTA is interleaved with content and "Rate"/"Volatility"/"Feed" are never defined.

audit.summary: This is a reference page whose entire purpose is to list on-chain contract addresses for Chainlink Rate and Volatility feeds — yet the served content contains **50 words, 0 tables, 0 numerals, and 0 hex identifiers**. The actual address data is almost certainly rendered client-side by a component the crawler never resolves, so what a generative engine ingests is a title, an empty "Networks" heading, and a newsletter signup. The metadata layer is genuinely strong (valid `TechArticle` + `BreadcrumbList` JSON-LD, canonical URL, full OG/Twitter tags), but it decorates a page with no extractable substance. The headline verdict: an engine cannot cite an address it cannot see — this page's dominant problem is that its core payload is invisible to retrieval, and no amount of prose polish fixes that.

recommendations.title: Server-render the address tables into the HTML
recommendations.issue: `## [Networks](#networks)` renders with zero following content; **0 hex identifiers** served
recommendations.change: Ensure per-network feed tables (feed name, proxy address `0x…`, decimals, chain) are present in the server-rendered DOM, not injected only by client-side JS. If a framework component builds them, add SSR/pre-render or an inline `<table>` fallback.
recommendations.why: Nothing here is retrievable or citable until the addresses exist in the crawled text — this is the gating fix for every other dimension.

recommendations.title: Emit each network's feeds as a real HTML `<table>`
recommendations.where: under `## Networks`, one H3 per network
recommendations.issue: **0 tables** measured on an inherently tabular page
recommendations.change: Structure as `### Ethereum Mainnet` → table with columns `Feed | Proxy Address | Asset/Name | Decimals`. Repeat per network. Each network becomes a clean RAG chunk.
recommendations.why: Tables are high-lift for extraction; per-network H3 sections give engines self-contained, quotable chunks keyed to the exact query ("address on [network]").

recommendations.title: Add symptom/query-phrased section leads
recommendations.where: intro paragraph and each network H3
recommendations.issue: page opens with two bare links, no answer sentence
recommendations.change: Lead with a liftable sentence, e.g. "The Chainlink Rate and Volatility feed proxy addresses for each supported network are listed below." Under each network, "Rate and Volatility feed addresses on {network}:".
recommendations.why: Matches how devs actually ask; gives an answer-first sentence an engine can quote even when the table is skimmed.

recommendations.title: Link each address to its block explorer
recommendations.where: the address column of each table
recommendations.change: Wrap each proxy address in an Etherscan/relevant-explorer link.
recommendations.why: Primary-source links raise credibility and citation rate, and let agents verify addresses.

recommendations.title: Add a one-line canonical definition of each feed type
recommendations.change: e.g. "Rate feeds report interest/exchange rates on-chain; Volatility feeds report implied or realized asset volatility." Add authoritative link to the concept page.
recommendations.why: Gives a crisp verbatim-liftable statement and improves entity resolution.

recommendations.title: Fix metadata freshness and entity signals
recommendations.issue: `dateModified` identical to `datePublished`; `keywords` include stopwords; `about` uses "Content about rate" template
recommendations.change: Stamp a real `dateModified` on address updates; replace auto-keywords with meaningful terms ("Chainlink Data Feeds", "proxy address", "Rate feed"); give `about` entries real descriptions.
recommendations.why: Visible freshness and clean entity data support E-E-A-T; low effort, but secondary to making the content exist.

antiPatterns: **Empty/near-empty rendered section:** `## Networks` heading with no server-rendered content — a wall of *absence*, the inverse of the usual wall-of-prose problem.
**Newsletter CTA interleaved with reference content:** "Get the latest Chainlink content straight to your inbox" appears as a heading in the content flow, diluting the chunk.
**Templated schema entities:** all `about` descriptions read "Content about X"; `keywords` contain stopwords.
offPageNotes: The page references `/llms.txt` as an agent index — good site-level practice; confirm this page's `.md` twin actually contains the address tables, since agents are told to "retrieve the smallest relevant .md page first."
The invisible-content issue is likely a site-wide client-side-rendering pattern affecting all address-listing pages; worth auditing SSR across `data-feeds/*/addresses`.
Raw `<head>` was provided and confirms strong metadata; the missing element is body content, not head tags.
